current.text: Trae Young is gone from Atlanta and the Hawks added no one to replace him, so the conditions behind his big role are still in place.
He is projected to start in the Atlanta backcourt with CJ McCollum and Dyson Daniels, at 30-plus minutes.
Experts expect him to keep his starting spot. Lu Dort is the threat to Atlanta guard minutes, but if Dort starts it would likely be in place of McCollum, not Alexander-Walker.
If Dort starts in place of McCollum, Alexander-Walker should get more shots and assists.
His role, minutes and time on the ball are seen as unchanged from last season and repeatable.

His second-half shooting run last season (about 70% true shooting, about 95% FT, mid-40s from three) will not hold. His pre All-Star level (about 20 points, 58% true shooting) is the better baseline, and that is still very good.
With McCollum on the roster for the full season and ball handling shared among several starters, his usage and ball handling may shift.
Lloyd projects him 35th in category leagues, well above his Yahoo rank of about 58, and calls him free real estate. Josh also says he goes 20 to 30 spots too low.
In auction terms, Josh values him in the mid 20s USD. He got him for 14 USD in a mock auction.
In snake drafts, round four or five is good value for him in 9-cat.
In points leagues his value only matches his ADP. That is why points rankings understate him for category leagues.
He turned more of his deflections into steals and got more deflections last season, so there may be room for more steals.
Atlanta is projected around 46 wins and fourth to eighth in the East. The team was not shutting players down late last season, and resting players is not a concern.
Atlanta plays 4-4-3 games in our playoff weeks 19 to 21 and has 14 back-to-backs.

durable.text: He has been one of the better catch-and-shoot three-point shooters in the NBA for three seasons. About 40% from three on high volume is a reasonable expectation.
His career FT% sat around 77 to 78% before he shot about 90% last season.
Experts treat the FT% jump as partly random. About 81% at the line would still be fine.
His best categories are threes, FT% and points. Rebounds and FG% are slightly below the pool, and no category is a weakness.

note: Experts see him as a top 35 to 50 category player. The market prices him far lower: Yahoo average cost is 4 USD against a Yahoo value of 17 USD and an ESPN value of 22 USD, and he went for 1 USD in our league last year. That makes him one of the best value buys in the auction. Bidding up to about 20 USD is supported, and Josh landed him at 14 USD in a mock. He has no weak category, so he fits any build, and he helps 3PM, FT% and PTS most. Early in the season, check three things: whether Dort cuts into his minutes, how his usage holds next to McCollum, and whether his FT% settles nearer 85 to 88% (projected) or drops back toward 80%.
